To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Ca2+ sequestration activity of SR from aged rats is reduced and that the Ca2+-pumping function of SL is increased.
the age-associated decline in the function of the cardiac Ca2+-pump of SR is not accompanied by a corresponding increase in the Ca(2+)-pump activity of SL.
the age-related decline in Ca2+ pump capacity of cardiac sarcoplamic reticulum was moderate at 1 year and became severe at 2 years of age.
In summary, our research is concerned with
age-related changes in cardiac function, and the mechanisms by which these changes are brought about.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
age-related decline in membrane Ca2+ pump functions of the cardiac SR and SL is a significant factor in the pathogenesis of age-related cardiac dysfunction.

the age-associated decline in the overall Ca2+ transport capacity of rat myocardial membranes was mainly due to the age-related decrease in the Ca2+-pump activity of SR, and not due to the increase in the Ca-ATPase activity of SL.
the age-associated decline in the rate of ATP-dependent Ca(2+) accumulation by the cardiac SR Ca(2+) pump is not a primary cause of age-related impairment in cardiac contractility.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Ca-ATPase pump activity of SR declines with age, while that of SL increases with age.
, with advancing age, the Ca2+ sequestrating function of cardiac SR is progressively compromised, whereas the Ca2+ transporting activity of cardiac SL is increased.
the Ca2+ transporting activities of SR and the sarcolemmal Ca2+ pump were both decreased in the myocardium of aged rats.
The main takeaway from our work is that
aging is associated with a decline in the Ca-ATPase activity of the sarcoplasmic (or endoplasmic) reticulum, which is a major intracellular Ca2+ store, but not the plasma membrane Ca2+ ATPase.
the Ca2+ sequestration capacity of the SR declines with aging, while that of the plasma membrane is increased.
the Ca2+ sequestration function of cardiac SR is progressively compromised with age whereas the Ca2+ extrusion function of cardiac sarcolemma is enhanced with age.
